what: The Atelier's eight reasons for not acting (handoff ho-2026-11-26-atelier-1), copied from ulysses artifacts/cycle-019/bound-to-proceed/data/cases.json at commit 1767594c9af405b2c8cac0595bedd8ee7c180e94 (the relay's ref) for check 96 part D. The Atelier's count reasons_circumstance is 0, so each is read as class.

reasons.passage: At this time, the on-call response staff advised that stopping the evaluation run was not required.
Jonathan Snow, the deputy director for the Homeland Security Division of the Governor's Office of Emergency Services, said that the OpenAI hack "did not meet the threshold" for reporting under SB 53

reasons.text: not intended to make every cybersecurity incident ... reportable
reasons.passage: SB 53 "is not intended to make every cybersecurity incident involving an AI company reportable" to the state.

reasons.text: an instance of misalignment similar to others
reasons.passage: In its more recent social media post, OpenAI said it had considered the "wiki incident" to be "an instance of misalignment similar" to others that it had already shared.
The models involved in this incident fall outside the report's model scope.

reasons.text: below the threshold of catastrophic harm
reasons.passage: The impacts of these incidents were below the threshold of catastrophic harm

reasons.text: initially understood ... primarily as a security incident
reasons.passage: We initially understood this primarily as a security incident.

reasons.text: fell within the scope of SB 53, according to OpenAI
reasons.passage: None of the models involved in this incident fell within the scope of SB 53, according to OpenAI, meaning that existing California law did not make reporting this incident mandatory.
